mechanics.name: Breakdown
mechanics.currentEffect: When you are unhooked by any means, that Hook breaks and the Killer's Aura is revealed to you for 4/5/6 seconds. The Hook repairs itself after 180 seconds.
activation: Ends/deactivates when: Killer Aura reveal ends after 4/5/6 seconds.
Ends/deactivates when: Hook repairs after 180 seconds.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.3.2): Reverted to the break-on-unhook version (Killer Aura 4/5/6 s, Hook repairs after 180 s) after the perk was disabled in 9.3.0.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Being unhooked breaks the Hook temporarily and briefly reveals the Killer.
specialInteractions: Broken Hook cannot be used until repaired.

editorial.summary: Whenever you are unhooked, destroy that Hook for 180 seconds and reveal the Killer's Aura to yourself for up to 6 seconds.
useCases: Create a temporary hook dead zone around the place you were rescued.
Use the Killer Aura read to route safely after the unhook.
Stack multiple copies or sabotage tools to make nearby future carries substantially harder.
counters: The Killer may have another hook within easy carrying distance.
The hook destruction matters only after you have already been hooked there.
Some maps have enough dense hook coverage that removing one hook changes little.
pros: Natural activation with no extra input.
Three-minute hook removal is extremely long.
cons: Can encourage anti-carry strategies that provoke slugging instead.
analysis: Breakdown ranks high in this band because 180 seconds is long enough for a destroyed hook to affect multiple later carries. Unlike a temporary sabotage, the hook remains unavailable through a large portion of the match after a completely natural unhook trigger.

The six-second Killer Aura read gives the perk independent post-unhook value even if the hook removal never matters. It helps the rescued Survivor understand whether the Killer is returning, rotating away, or cutting off an escape route.

The ceiling rises sharply when the map already has awkward hook spacing or when teammates also bring Breakout and Saboteur. Removing a key hook can force long carry routes, create pallet-save opportunities, or convince the Killer to abandon a pickup.

The ranking stays in B because hook density is outside the Survivor's control. Some maps give the Killer another hook a few steps away. Breakdown is easy to use and occasionally vicious, but not consistently decisive.
editorial.verdict: An underrated hook-denial perk with a useful information bonus. Breakdown can quietly ruin a carry zone for three full minutes, but map geometry decides how painful that really is.
